newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK govt sees 96 inflation at 6.5 pct - Chan quoted.
newsitem.headline: HK govt sees 96 inflation at 6.5 pct - Chan quoted.

text.p: Hong Kong's inflation rate was expected to fall to 6.5 percent this year and even lower next year, Hong Kong Chief Secretary Anson Chan told Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda on Wednesday.
A Japanese foreign ministry official quoted Chan as saying Hong Kong's economic fundamentals were very strong.
"She said that she expected five percent growth, and the inflation figures were coming down (to) 6.5 percent this year and lower next year," the official told reporters.
The Hong Kong government officially forecasts 1996 inflation at 7.5 percent against 8.7 percent last year.

But consumer price index (A), the territory's most broadly based inflation figure, has averaged around 6.4 percent in the first seven months of the year, and the government is widely expected to revise its full-year forecast soon.
Hong Kong Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said last week that inflation in the territory was under control and could go lower for the rest of 1996.
He was quoted on government radio as saying the official forecast might be revised downward, but did not say what the new estimate would be.

The Japanese foreign ministry official also quoted Chan as saying during her one hour meeting this afternoon with Ikeda that consumption and activities in the stock and real estate markets were picking up.
Ikeda is visiting Hong Kong to exchange views on the territory's transition to Chinese sovereignty next year.
